out:
name: Console CI - Build (CLI Executables)

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      next_version:
        type: string
        required: false

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
# This is a reusable workflow. A callee can never exceed what the calling job
# grants, so each job's block below is also the contract its callers must meet.
permissions: {}

# Note: Renet binaries are built by ci-build-renet.yml and downloaded as artifact
# This workflow depends on build-renet completing first (configured in ci.yml)

jobs:
  build-cli-executables:
    name: CLI (${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    # Checkout and artifacts only. No GitHub API, no registry, no git remote.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      # fail-fast: false, and the reason is diagnostic rather than stylistic.
      # GitHub's matrix fail-fast cancels every sibling the moment one leg fails,
      # BEFORE the watchdog is ever consulted, so a cancelled sibling never
      # reaches a verdict and never appears in the watchdog's failure roster. On
      # a branch being driven to green that turns each round into one failure
      # instead of the whole surface, which is the exact serialisation this
      # program is trying to remove. Its siblings ci-build-docker.yml and
      # ci-build-renet.yml already set it; these two were the odd ones out.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux
            arch: x64
            timeout: 5
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 6
          - os: macos-latest
            platform: mac
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 5
          - os: macos-15-intel
            platform: mac
            arch: x64
            timeout: 10
          - os: windows-latest
            platform: win
            arch: x64
            timeout: 6
          - os: windows-11-arm
            platform: win
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 15
          # Musl-linked Linux binaries (for Alpine/musl distros)
          # Built inside node:24-alpine Docker container on Ubuntu runners
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux-musl
            arch: x64
            timeout: 7
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux-musl
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Download full renet binaries (with embedded CRIU/rsync) from unified build
      - name: Download renet binaries
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: renet-binaries-${{ github.sha }}
          path: private/bin/

      # Native build steps (skip for musl — handled inside Docker)
      #
      # The explicit `--ignore-scripts` on Windows is gone, not lost:
      # install-deps.sh adds it itself when CI_OS is windows (common.sh exports
      # CI_OS), so the flag was already redundant at the call site. The cache key
      # in setup-workspace carries runner.os, so the Windows tree (built with
      # --ignore-scripts) can never be served to a Linux job.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-workspace
        if: matrix.platform != 'linux-musl'
        with:
          build-packages: 'true'

      # RELEASE GATE. next_version is declared `required: false`, and both build
      # steps below used to spell `${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}`,
      # so a release run whose version never resolved would build and upload a
      # placeholder-versioned SEA and nothing would object. This step makes the
      # --strict path of inject-env.sh reachable: on push-to-main -- the only
      # event whose artifacts CD ever promotes -- an empty, placeholder, or
      # malformed version fails the job before anything is built. PR runs skip
      # it and keep the 0.0.0-dev fallback.
      - name: Require a real version on the release path
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        shell: bash
        env:
          NEXT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.version.inject_env --version "$NEXT_VERSION" --strict --print

      - name: Build CLI SEA executable
        if: matrix.platform != 'linux-musl'
        shell: bash
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.build.build_cli_executables --platform ${{ matrix.platform }} --arch ${{ matrix.arch }}
        env:
          CLI_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}
          # Makes the build script re-check the version with --strict and refuse
          # a placeholder, right where the bytes are stamped.
          RELEASE_BUILD: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # Musl build (runs entire build inside Alpine Docker container)
      - name: Build CLI SEA executable (musl)
        if: matrix.platform == 'linux-musl'
        shell: bash
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.build.build_cli_musl --arch ${{ matrix.arch }}
        env:
          CLI_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}
          RELEASE_BUILD: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: build-cli-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ matrix.arch }}-${{ github.sha }}
          path: dist/cli/
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: error

name: Claude Mention

# Interactive @claude on PRs and issues. PUBLIC repo: only privileged humans
# may summon Claude (author_association gate); the Bot-type check keeps
# bot-authored comments (review markers, Claude's own replies) from
# re-triggering regardless of association. Comment-only by design:
# contents stays read (flipping it to write would let "@claude fix this"
# push to PR branches -- an explicit operator decision, not a default).

on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

# Queue (not cancel) per issue/PR: a second mention must not kill a running
# answer.
concurrency:
  group: claude-mention-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  claude:
    name: Claude
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: >-
      contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude') &&
      github.event.comment.user.type != 'Bot' &&
      contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association)
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      actions: read # lets Claude read CI results when asked about failures
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # SHADOW RUN: exports BWS_-prefixed copies that nothing consumes. The
        # live secrets.* reads below are untouched until the cutover flips them.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN > BWS_ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN

      # No `prompt:` input -> interactive/tag mode; default trigger_phrase is
      # @claude. Same token strategy as claude-review.yml.
      - name: Run Claude
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@fa7e2f0a29a126f0b81cdcf360561b36e44cf608 # v1.0.180
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ env.BWS_ANTHROPIC_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
          claude_args: --model claude-sonnet-5

name: Console CT - Update Flow

# End-to-end tests for install.sh + `rdc update` lifecycle. Runs the
# real rdc binary against a local Python HTTP fixture server that serves
# controlled manifest.json / latest.json / binary / .sha256 under
# /cli/<channel>/... . Validates:
#   - install.sh lays down the single-bin/rdc layout
#   - `rdc update` swaps binary, creates .old, updates state
#   - check-only, sha256 mismatch, rollback, channel switch semantics
#   - re-install migrates legacy versions/ + cleans staged-update
#
# Reusable so the caller workflow (ci.yml) can decide when to run it.
# Expects a rdc binary built upstream; consumed via actions/download-artifact.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      cli_artifact_name:
        description: 'Name of the uploaded artifact containing the rdc binary'
        required: true
        type: string
      cli_artifact_binary:
        description: 'Filename of the rdc binary inside the artifact (e.g., rdc-linux-x64)'
        required: true
        type: string

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
# This is a reusable workflow. A callee can never exceed what the calling job
# grants, so each job's block below is also the contract its callers must meet.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  # Linux x64 is the primary matrix cell because it covers the full install.sh
  # code path + the most common rdc binary. macOS / Windows parity are
  # follow-up work tracked in the PR plan.
  test-linux-x64:
    name: Update flow (Linux x64)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Checkout, artifact download, and a local fixture server. No GitHub API.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download rdc binary
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.cli_artifact_name }}
          path: /tmp/rdc-artifact

      - name: Locate rdc
        id: rdc
        run: |
          RDC="/tmp/rdc-artifact/${{ inputs.cli_artifact_binary }}"
          if [[ ! -f "$RDC" ]]; then
            echo "::error::rdc binary not found at $RDC"
            ls -la /tmp/rdc-artifact || true
            exit 1
          fi
          chmod +x "$RDC"
          echo "path=$RDC" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Run update-flow scenarios
        env:
          RDC_BINARY: ${{ steps.rdc.outputs.path }}
        run: |
          PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.testrun.rdc_update all

name: Runner Profiler
description: >
  Sample this job's CPU / RAM / disk / network and append a per-minute profile
  to the job's summary panel, so runner sizing is a measurement rather than a
  guess.

  WHY. Standard runners are free and unlimited on this public repo, so an
  oversized runner costs no money and roughly 4x the core-minutes: a job that
  uses ~1 core on a 4-vCPU ubuntu-latest VM burns four cores' worth of the
  world's electricity to do one core's work. ubuntu-slim is 1 vCPU / 5 GB /
  14 GB disk with a HARD 15-minute job cap, and the point of this action is to
  find every job that fits it.

  MECHANISM. `runs.post` is JavaScript-actions-only (composite actions have no
  equivalent) and `post-if` defaults to always(), so `main` starts a detached
  bash sampler and `post` stops it and writes the panel EVEN WHEN THE JOB
  FAILS. The action carries no npm dependencies at all: it runs on the runner's
  own bundled node using stdlib only.

  PLACEMENT. A summary panel's title is the job's `name:`, and all of a job's
  step summaries concatenate into that one panel, so this APPENDS a section to
  the job's own panel. It cannot create a separately-titled one.

inputs:
  interval:
    description: >
      Seconds between samples. The default is deliberately at the slow end of
      the 5-10s band: on a 1-vCPU slim runner the profiler competes with the
      work it is measuring, and a profiler that perturbs its subject is
      measuring itself.
    required: false
    default: '10'
  strict:
    description: >
      'true' makes a degenerate profile FAIL the job. A degenerate profile means
      nothing was sampled, every CPU reading was zero, every RAM reading was
      identical, or the sampler read host-sized limits from inside a container
      (HOST_LEAK) -- each of which would otherwise print a clean-looking zero
      profile that someone could move a job on.

      Default false. The repo bans the step keyword that swallows a failure, so
      soft behaviour has to be a real input rather than a shrug in the workflow,
      and a bug in a brand-new observability tool must not turn CI red. It flips
      to true once the profiler has run clean across the job matrix; until then
      the findings are ::warning:: annotations.
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  runner-label:
    description: >
      The runner label this job actually requested, e.g. ubuntu-slim. This ARMS
      the HOST_LEAK check: inside slim's unprivileged container `nproc` and
      /proc/meminfo report the HOST, so a failed cgroup read yields 4 cores /
      16 GB on a 1-core / 5 GB runner, and every conclusion drawn from it is
      wrong in the dangerous direction. With the label present the sampler
      refuses to profile at all; without it the check cannot fire, so pass it.
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  # node20 is deprecated on GitHub runners (forced onto Node 24 with a warning
  # in every job since 2025-09); declare what actually runs.
  using: node24
  main: index.js
  # Explicit even though always() is the default: this hook exists precisely to
  # profile the runs that fail, and a silent default is not worth relying on.
  post: index.js
  post-if: always()

name: Profiler Probe

# Answer, from a real runner, the three questions that cannot be settled by
# reading anything:
#
#   1. What does a job INSIDE the ubuntu-slim container actually see? slim is an
#      unprivileged container, not a VM, so `nproc` and /proc/meminfo report the
#      HOST. Whether /sys/fs/cgroup is readable there, and at which version,
#      decides whether the profiler can size anything at all or is quietly
#      reading 4 cores / 16 GB on a 1-core / 5 GB box.
#   2. Does a JavaScript action's `post:` hook still fire when the action is
#      NESTED inside a composite action? If yes, one line in setup-workspace
#      covers 26 jobs. If no, every job needs an explicit edit. The direct jobs
#      below are the CONTROL: without them, "no panel" cannot be told apart from
#      "the action is broken everywhere".
#   3. What does a sample really cost on 1 vCPU? The loop is fork-free precisely
#      to stay out of the way of the work it measures; that claim is timed here
#      over 100 iterations rather than asserted.
#
# workflow_dispatch ONLY, and every job is read-only: it checks out the repo,
# reads /proc and /sys, times a loop, and writes to its own job summary. It
# mutates nothing, holds no secrets, and is safe to dispatch at any time.
#
# READING THE RESULT: each job's summary panel gets a "Runner probe" section
# from the facts jobs, and a "Runner Profile" section IF AND ONLY IF the post
# hook fired. Compare post-direct against post-nested to answer question 2.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  facts-slim:
    name: Facts (ubuntu-slim)
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    # ubuntu-slim's 15-minute cap is a CANCELLATION, not a failure: it reads as
    # neither pass nor fail and poisons anything aggregating it. An explicit
    # timeout under the cap turns it into an ordinary, legible failure.
    timeout-minutes: 14
    # Checkout + runner-local profiler only. index.js makes zero network
    # calls; the step summary and ::warning:: are runner-side, not API calls.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            .ci/scripts
            .ci/rediacc_ci

      - name: Probe runner facts
        run: .ci/scripts/ci/profiler/sampler_linux.py --probe
        env:
          PROFILER_RUNNER_LABEL: ubuntu-slim

  facts-latest:
    name: Facts (ubuntu-latest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same as facts-slim: checkout + profiler. "post" here is the JS action
    # post-step hook, not posting anything to GitHub.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            .ci/scripts
            .ci/rediacc_ci

      - name: Probe runner facts
        run: .ci/scripts/ci/profiler/sampler_linux.py --probe
        env:
          PROFILER_RUNNER_LABEL: ubuntu-latest

  post-direct-latest:
    name: Post hook, direct (ubuntu-latest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same as facts-slim: checkout + profiler. "post" here is the JS action
    # post-step hook, not posting anything to GitHub.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler
        with:
          interval: '5'
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Burn one core for 40s
        run: timeout 40 bash -c 'while :; do :; done' || true

  post-nested-latest:
    name: Post hook, nested in a composite (ubuntu-latest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same as facts-slim: checkout + profiler. "post" here is the JS action
    # post-step hook, not posting anything to GitHub.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler/nest-probe
        with:
          interval: '5'
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Burn one core for 40s
        run: timeout 40 bash -c 'while :; do :; done' || true

  post-nested-slim:
    name: Post hook, nested in a composite (ubuntu-slim)
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 14
    # Same as facts-slim: checkout + profiler. "post" here is the JS action
    # post-step hook, not posting anything to GitHub.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler/nest-probe
        with:
          interval: '5'
          runner-label: ubuntu-slim

      - name: Burn one core for 40s
        run: timeout 40 bash -c 'while :; do :; done' || true

name: Nightly Status

run-name: "Nightly status: run ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }} (${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }})"

# Reports the nightly's verdict somewhere a human will actually see it.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. `ci.yml` sets `full_suite: github.event_name != 'push'`, so
# push-to-main skips the expensive suites on the grounds that the PR already
# validated them. That makes the 01:00 UTC nightly the ONLY thing validating
# main -- and a scheduled run that fails at 01:00 notifies nobody, appears in no
# PR, and blocks nothing. Measured 2026-07-27: twelve consecutive `cancelled`
# nightlies, zero successes, back to 2026-07-16, entirely unnoticed.
#
# WHY A SEPARATE WORKFLOW rather than a branch inside watchdog-monitor.yml:
#   - Opening an issue needs `issues: write`. The watchdog runs on EVERY CI run
#     (many times per PR); this runs once a night. Granting the write here keeps
#     it off the hot path.
#   - No `.github/actions/app-token` preset grants `issues` (readonly, pr-read,
#     push, cd, housekeeping), and that wrapper is deliberately narrow because
#     the app holds an `always` bypass on the main ruleset. The built-in
#     `github.token` with a job-scoped grant is the smaller change: it cannot
#     bypass the ruleset, and issues it creates do not trigger further workflows.
#   - The watchdog is a chained poller that exits mid-run; the final conclusion
#     is only knowable from `workflow_run: completed`, which is a different
#     trigger entirely.
#
# TESTING NOTE, and it is a real limitation: `workflow_run` always executes the
# workflow file from the DEFAULT BRANCH. This file therefore cannot run from a
# PR, and its first real execution is after merge, on the next nightly. The
# logic it calls is unit-tested; the wiring is not testable pre-merge.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Console CI"]
    types: [completed]

# No default; the reporting job declares issues: write for itself.
# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

# Serialise per run so a rerun's completion cannot race the first report and
# double-post. Never cancel: a dropped report is the whole failure mode here.
concurrency:
  group: nightly-status-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  report:
    name: Report nightly verdict
    # Scheduled runs only. Every other event has a human attached to it already.
    if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read    # list the failed jobs of the run being reported on
      issues: write    # open, comment on and close the rolling nightly-red issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # .ci/config for ci-alerts.json, the handles a red night @mentions.
          sparse-checkout: |
            .ci/scripts
            .ci/config

      - name: Report nightly verdict
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3  # v9.0.0
        env:
          NIGHTLY_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          NIGHTLY_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
          NIGHTLY_EVENT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
          NIGHTLY_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
        with:
          script: return await require('./.ci/scripts/ci/report-nightly-status.cjs')({github, context, core})

name: Cleanup PR Channel

# Delete R2 channel artifacts when a PR is closed (merged or abandoned)

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

jobs:
  cleanup:
    name: Delete PR Channel
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Checkout only. The delete is against R2 with Bitwarden credentials;
    # no GitHub API call in this job.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same fork guard as cleanup-preview.yml. This job holds R2 delete
    # credentials for the releases bucket; a fork PR has empty secrets, so the
    # step would fail into `|| true` and log a confusing no-op. Fork PRs are
    # unsupported (see .github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    steps:
      # The logic now lives in .ci/scripts/deploy/delete-r2-channel.sh, so the
      # repo has to be on disk. Sparse, but a sparse cone is a SECOND dependency
      # graph: the bws-secrets step below `uses:` a local composite resolved from
      # the WORKSPACE, so the action itself and the map it reads must be in the
      # cone too, or the step fails with the action simply not there.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # .ci/rediacc_ci, because the step(s) below run `python3 -m rediacc_ci.*` and a cone that stops at .ci/scripts does not put that package on disk at all: the job dies with ModuleNotFoundError before judging anything, and a crash is not a verdict. Added 2026-09-21, sweeping the class the ci-complete cone was found in.
          sparse-checkout: |
            .ci/scripts
            .ci/config
            .github/actions
            .ci/rediacc_ci

      - name: Load well-known
        run: grep '^WK_' .ci/config/well-known.env >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # SHADOW RUN: exports BWS_-prefixed copies that nothing consumes. The
        # live secrets.* reads below are untouched until the cutover flips them.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
      - name: Delete channel artifacts
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.deploy.delete_r2_channel
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: auto
          CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT }}
          RELEASES_BUCKET: ${{ env.WK_RELEASES_BUCKET }}

name: CI - OBS Mirror

# The openSUSE Leap 16.0 Ceph mirror (agent/plans/PLAN-renet-obs-mirror.md, D2).
# OBS filesystems:ceph:squid/16.0 keeps only its latest build, and renet pins
# one exact EVR, so every build is captured while OBS still serves it: the
# signed OBS repodata unmodified plus the RPMs renet installs from it, one tar
# in ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake tagged obs-mirror-v1-opensuse-16.0-<EVR>.
# A tag that exists is never rewritten. rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror proves
# each capture in containers with OBS unreachable before it pushes. Main only:
# pull requests read the package and never write it.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - private/renet
      - .ci/rediacc_ci/infra/obs_mirror.py
      - .github/workflows/ci-obs-mirror.yml
  # A PR that touches the pin or this tool captures on its own CI, so the pinned
  # build is mirrored before merge (workflow_dispatch only runs from main).
  # Same-repo PRs only: the job's `if` skips forks, whose token cannot write.
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - private/renet
      - .ci/rediacc_ci/infra/obs_mirror.py
      - .github/workflows/ci-obs-mirror.yml
  schedule:
    # OBS replaces a build in the same publish that adds the next; every 6 hours
    # catches each build while it is still served (plan Q3).
    - cron: '23 */6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      evr:
        description: 'EVR to capture instead of the one OBS serves now (e.g. 19.2.3-lp160.2.97)'
        required: false
        default: ''

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: ci-obs-mirror
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  capture:
    name: OBS Mirror (opensuse-16.0)
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # packages: write pushes to ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake with github.token.
    # The package is already private (ci-vm-bake.yml, ruling D1), so the mirror
    # tags inherit that and never publish Ceph binaries.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler
        with:
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # LIVE: the BWS_ values below are read by this job's steps.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY > BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
            DOCKERHUB_TOKEN > BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN
            DOCKERHUB_USERNAME > BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME
            GITHUB_APP_ID > BWS_APP_ID
      - uses: ./.github/actions/app-token
        id: app-token
        with:
          client-id: ${{ env.BWS_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ env.BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          preset: readonly
          repositories: console,renet
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
      # renet alone: the OBS key, the pin, the package names and the binary all come from it.
      - name: Init renet submodule
        run: git submodule update --init --depth 1 private/renet

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}
      # opensuse/leap:16.0 comes from Docker Hub.
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          username: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Install oras
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image install-oras

      - name: Read the build OBS serves
        id: upstream
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror upstream

      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: 'stable'
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: private/renet/go.sum
      # A plain static `go build`, as the pkg matrix does: `renet ceph install`
      # needs no embedded assets, and the binary runs in the Leap container.
      # Never uploaded (console is public).
      - name: Build renet
        working-directory: private/renet
        run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet" ./cmd/renet

      # OBS's current build, pinned or not: capturing it before the pin moves is
      # what lets the pin move at all.
      - name: Capture the build OBS serves
        env:
          OBS_MIRROR_EVR: ${{ inputs.evr || steps.upstream.outputs.obs_evr }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror capture --evr "$OBS_MIRROR_EVR" --renet "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet"
      # The tree's pin: a no-op once captured, and red when it is neither
      # captured nor served any more.
      - name: Capture the pin
        if: steps.upstream.outputs.pin != (inputs.evr || steps.upstream.outputs.obs_evr)
        env:
          OBS_MIRROR_EVR: ${{ steps.upstream.outputs.pin }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror capture --evr "$OBS_MIRROR_EVR" --renet "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet"

name: Claude Review

# Thin caller: all review mechanics live in claude-review-reusable.yml (the
# single source shared with the submodule repos' callers). Console keeps its
# two entry points -- Console CI green while ready, and the ready-flip itself
# -- and its "CI Complete" green gate. INVARIANT (operator ruling
# 2026-07-22): a review fires ONLY for a non-draft PR whose CURRENT head has
# green CI at decision time; the authoritative gating (same-SHA marker dedup,
# pointer-bump skip) lives in the gate script inside the reusable.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Console CI"]
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [ready_for_review]
  # Manual escape hatch (found 2026-07-30, PR #546 run 30572143752): the
  # workflow_run delivery above has been observed to silently not fire for a
  # green PR-branch "Console CI" completion, with no run of any conclusion
  # recorded, leaving the review-status check red with no path to recover. The gate
  # script and reusable already had a workflow_dispatch/pr_number code path
  # (`claude-review-gate.sh`'s `pull_request | workflow_dispatch` case); only
  # this trigger declaration was missing. Same safety invariant applies: the
  # gate script re-checks required_check (CI Complete) is green on the
  # CURRENT head before reviewing anything.
  #
  # `gh workflow run` MUST carry `--ref <branch>` while this trigger is
  # unmerged: GitHub resolves whether a workflow ACCEPTS workflow_dispatch
  # from the DEFAULT BRANCH's copy of this file. (This comment used to add
  # "and which YAML defines the job". That half is wrong -- the run uses the
  # version at the event's own ref, so the dispatched BRANCH's copy executes;
  # acceptance and execution resolve against different refs. See the dispatch
  # section of docs/agent-reference/ci-gates.md.) Without --ref,
  # `gh workflow run claude-review.yml -f pr_number=N`
  # fails closed with a 422 ("Workflow does not have 'workflow_dispatch'
  # trigger") because main does not have this block yet. Observed live: PR
  # #546 run 30588087212. Once this trigger merges to main the flag becomes
  # optional (defaults to main, which is then correct), but --ref remains
  # the safe form for dispatching against a branch's OWN in-flight review.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: 'PR number to manually re-review (use when workflow_run does not fire)'
        required: true
        type: string
      model:
        description: 'Model for this review round.'
        required: false
        type: choice
        default: 'claude-sonnet-5'
        options: ['claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-opus-5']

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

# One review pipeline per head branch; a newer green push supersedes an
# in-flight review of the old head. workflow_dispatch has no branch/ref in
# its event payload, so it gets its own group keyed by the PR number instead
# of colliding with (and cancelling) the automatic pipeline for that branch.
concurrency:
  group: claude-review-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || github.event.pull_request.head.ref || format('dispatch-{0}', inputs.pr_number) }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  review:
    # Pre-filter only; the authoritative decision is the gate script. Fork
    # guard: workflow_run executes in base-repo context WITH secrets.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
       github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
       github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    # A called workflow cannot exceed the CALLER's grant, and this workflow's
    # top-level default is contents:read — so without restating them here the
    # reusable's pull-requests/issues/checks requests exceed the caller and
    # GitHub fails the run at startup with no job and no log (observed: run
    # 30064158589, startup_failure). Job-level keeps the widening scoped to
    # the review call instead of raising the whole workflow's default.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      checks: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/claude-review-reusable.yml
    with:
      required_check: CI Complete
      pr_number: ${{ inputs.pr_number || '' }}
      # Empty on the two automatic entry points, where the reusable's own
      # default applies; only a manual re-review can pick a different model.
      model: ${{ inputs.model || 'claude-sonnet-5' }}
    secrets:
      BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

name: CI - VM Bake

# Pre-baked E2E VM images (agent/plans/PLAN-ci-prebaked-vm-images.md, box B4).
# One leg per distro computes the bake key (rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_key), stops
# at the probe when ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake already holds that tag, and
# otherwise runs `renet ops image build --bake-key` and pushes the image under
# the key. ct-tests.yml's E2E Workers legs pull it by the same key and fall back
# to the stock image on a miss. Main only: pull requests read the package and
# never write it.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - private/renet
      - .ci/rediacc_ci/infra/vm_bake_key.py
      - .ci/rediacc_ci/infra/vm_bake_image.py
      - .github/workflows/ci-vm-bake.yml
  schedule:
    # The key carries the month, so the 1st needs a fresh set.
    - cron: '0 2 1 * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Every job below declares its own permissions, so this workflow-level default
# is deliberately empty: a job added without a block gets nothing and fails
# loudly, rather than silently inheriting a scope nobody audited it for.
permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: ci-vm-bake-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  bake:
    name: VM Bake (${{ matrix.os-image }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # packages: write pushes the baked image to ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake with
    # github.token. The first push (run 36670172753) created the package PUBLIC,
    # inheriting this public repository's visibility; the operator set it private
    # on 2026-09-30 (ruling D1) through the package settings page, the only place
    # that changes it, since no API sets package visibility.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os-image:
          - ubuntu-24.04
          - debian-13
          - fedora-43
          - opensuse-16.0
          - oracle-10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler
        with:
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # LIVE: the BWS_ values below are read by this job's steps.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY > BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
            DOCKERHUB_TOKEN > BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN
            DOCKERHUB_USERNAME > BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME
            GITHUB_APP_ID > BWS_APP_ID
      - uses: ./.github/actions/app-token
        id: app-token
        with:
          client-id: ${{ env.BWS_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ env.BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          preset: readonly
          repositories: console,renet
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
      # renet alone: the key hashes its sources and the build needs nothing else.
      - name: Init renet submodule
        run: git submodule update --init --depth 1 private/renet

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Install oras
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image install-oras
      # The early exit: a key that already has a package ends the leg here.
      - name: Probe the bake key
        id: probe
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image probe --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}"

      - name: Free Disk Space (start)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          username: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        with:
          go-version: 'stable'
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: private/renet/go.sum
      # Same staged embed-assets cache as the E2E Workers legs (ci-build-renet.yml
      # writes it); restore only, the bake never saves it.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: embed-cache
        with:
          path: private/renet/pkg/embed/assets
          key: renet-embed-assets-${{ hashFiles('private/renet/embed-assets.lock.json') }}
      - name: Pre-pull Docker base images (avoid buildx auth issues)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false' && steps.embed-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.docker_prepull debian:bookworm=linux/amd64 debian:bookworm-slim=linux/arm64 ubuntu:24.04=linux/amd64 ubuntu:24.04=linux/arm64
      - name: Build renet
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.build_renet --nolicense
      - name: Install renet
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: sudo cp "$RENET_BINARY" /usr/bin/renet && sudo chmod +x /usr/bin/renet

      # The stock base image, from the cache the E2E Workers legs save (same key).
      # Restore only: on a miss the builder downloads it, and the E2E legs own the save.
      - name: Compute VM image cache key
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: vm-image-key
        run: echo "key=vm-base-image-e2e-${{ matrix.os-image }}-$(date -u +%Y-%m)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Restore VM base image cache
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/renet/disks
          key: ${{ steps.vm-image-key.outputs.key }}

      - name: Free Disk Space (wait)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space
        with:
          mode: wait
      - name: Setup KVM Host
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: sudo "$RENET_BINARY" ops host setup

      - name: Bake the image
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: build
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image build --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}" --key "${{ steps.probe.outputs.key }}" --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet/disks-baked" --renet /usr/bin/renet
      - name: Publish to GHCR
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image publish --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}" --key "${{ steps.probe.outputs.key }}" --image "${{ steps.build.outputs.image }}"

name: CLI (${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ matrix.arch }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    # Checkout and artifacts only. No GitHub API, no registry, no git remote.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      # fail-fast: false, and the reason is diagnostic rather than stylistic.
      # GitHub's matrix fail-fast cancels every sibling the moment one leg fails,
      # BEFORE the watchdog is ever consulted, so a cancelled sibling never
      # reaches a verdict and never appears in the watchdog's failure roster. On
      # a branch being driven to green that turns each round into one failure
      # instead of the whole surface, which is the exact serialisation this
      # program is trying to remove. Its siblings ci-build-docker.yml and
      # ci-build-renet.yml already set it; these two were the odd ones out.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux
            arch: x64
            timeout: 5
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 6
          - os: macos-latest
            platform: mac
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 5
          - os: macos-15-intel
            platform: mac
            arch: x64
            timeout: 10
          - os: windows-latest
            platform: win
            arch: x64
            timeout: 6
          - os: windows-11-arm
            platform: win
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 15
          # Musl-linked Linux binaries (for Alpine/musl distros)
          # Built inside node:24-alpine Docker container on Ubuntu runners
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            platform: linux-musl
            arch: x64
            timeout: 7
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux-musl
            arch: arm64
            timeout: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Download full renet binaries (with embedded CRIU/rsync) from unified build
      - name: Download renet binaries
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: renet-binaries-${{ github.sha }}
          path: private/bin/

      # Native build steps (skip for musl — handled inside Docker)
      #
      # The explicit `--ignore-scripts` on Windows is gone, not lost:
      # install-deps.sh adds it itself when CI_OS is windows (common.sh exports
      # CI_OS), so the flag was already redundant at the call site. The cache key
      # in setup-workspace carries runner.os, so the Windows tree (built with
      # --ignore-scripts) can never be served to a Linux job.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-workspace
        if: matrix.platform != 'linux-musl'
        with:
          build-packages: 'true'

      # RELEASE GATE. next_version is declared `required: false`, and both build
      # steps below used to spell `${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}`,
      # so a release run whose version never resolved would build and upload a
      # placeholder-versioned SEA and nothing would object. This step makes the
      # --strict path of inject-env.sh reachable: on push-to-main -- the only
      # event whose artifacts CD ever promotes -- an empty, placeholder, or
      # malformed version fails the job before anything is built. PR runs skip
      # it and keep the 0.0.0-dev fallback.
      - name: Require a real version on the release path
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        shell: bash
        env:
          NEXT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.version.inject_env --version "$NEXT_VERSION" --strict --print

      - name: Build CLI SEA executable
        if: matrix.platform != 'linux-musl'
        shell: bash
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.build.build_cli_executables --platform ${{ matrix.platform }} --arch ${{ matrix.arch }}
        env:
          CLI_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}
          # Makes the build script re-check the version with --strict and refuse
          # a placeholder, right where the bytes are stamped.
          RELEASE_BUILD: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      # Musl build (runs entire build inside Alpine Docker container)
      - name: Build CLI SEA executable (musl)
        if: matrix.platform == 'linux-musl'
        shell: bash
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.build.build_cli_musl --arch ${{ matrix.arch }}
        env:
          CLI_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next_version || '0.0.0-dev' }}
          RELEASE_BUILD: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: build-cli-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ matrix.arch }}-${{ github.sha }}
          path: dist/cli/
          retention-days: 3
          if-no-files-found: error

# Pre-filter only; the authoritative decision is the gate script. Fork
    # guard: workflow_run executes in base-repo context WITH secrets.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
       github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
       github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    # A called workflow cannot exceed the CALLER's grant, and this workflow's
    # top-level default is contents:read — so without restating them here the
    # reusable's pull-requests/issues/checks requests exceed the caller and
    # GitHub fails the run at startup with no job and no log (observed: run
    # 30064158589, startup_failure). Job-level keeps the widening scoped to
    # the review call instead of raising the whole workflow's default.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      checks: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/claude-review-reusable.yml
    with:
      required_check: CI Complete
      pr_number: ${{ inputs.pr_number || '' }}
      # Empty on the two automatic entry points, where the reusable's own
      # default applies; only a manual re-review can pick a different model.
      model: ${{ inputs.model || 'claude-sonnet-5' }}
    secrets:
      BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}

name: Delete PR Channel
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Checkout only. The delete is against R2 with Bitwarden credentials;
    # no GitHub API call in this job.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same fork guard as cleanup-preview.yml. This job holds R2 delete
    # credentials for the releases bucket; a fork PR has empty secrets, so the
    # step would fail into `|| true` and log a confusing no-op. Fork PRs are
    # unsupported (see .github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    steps:
      # The logic now lives in .ci/scripts/deploy/delete-r2-channel.sh, so the
      # repo has to be on disk. Sparse, but a sparse cone is a SECOND dependency
      # graph: the bws-secrets step below `uses:` a local composite resolved from
      # the WORKSPACE, so the action itself and the map it reads must be in the
      # cone too, or the step fails with the action simply not there.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # .ci/rediacc_ci, because the step(s) below run `python3 -m rediacc_ci.*` and a cone that stops at .ci/scripts does not put that package on disk at all: the job dies with ModuleNotFoundError before judging anything, and a crash is not a verdict. Added 2026-09-21, sweeping the class the ci-complete cone was found in.
          sparse-checkout: |
            .ci/scripts
            .ci/config
            .github/actions
            .ci/rediacc_ci

      - name: Load well-known
        run: grep '^WK_' .ci/config/well-known.env >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # SHADOW RUN: exports BWS_-prefixed copies that nothing consumes. The
        # live secrets.* reads below are untouched until the cutover flips them.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT
            CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY > BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
      - name: Delete channel artifacts
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.deploy.delete_r2_channel
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: auto
          CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT: ${{ env.BWS_CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT }}
          RELEASES_BUCKET: ${{ env.WK_RELEASES_BUCKET }}
          CHANNEL: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

name: Update flow (Linux x64)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Checkout, artifact download, and a local fixture server. No GitHub API.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download rdc binary
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c  # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.cli_artifact_name }}
          path: /tmp/rdc-artifact

      - name: Locate rdc
        id: rdc
        run: |
          RDC="/tmp/rdc-artifact/${{ inputs.cli_artifact_binary }}"
          if [[ ! -f "$RDC" ]]; then
            echo "::error::rdc binary not found at $RDC"
            ls -la /tmp/rdc-artifact || true
            exit 1
          fi
          chmod +x "$RDC"
          echo "path=$RDC" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Run update-flow scenarios
        env:
          RDC_BINARY: ${{ steps.rdc.outputs.path }}
        run: |
          PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.testrun.rdc_update all

name: OBS Mirror (opensuse-16.0)
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # packages: write pushes to ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake with github.token.
    # The package is already private (ci-vm-bake.yml, ruling D1), so the mirror
    # tags inherit that and never publish Ceph binaries.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler
        with:
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # LIVE: the BWS_ values below are read by this job's steps.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY > BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
            DOCKERHUB_TOKEN > BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN
            DOCKERHUB_USERNAME > BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME
            GITHUB_APP_ID > BWS_APP_ID
      - uses: ./.github/actions/app-token
        id: app-token
        with:
          client-id: ${{ env.BWS_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ env.BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          preset: readonly
          repositories: console,renet
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
      # renet alone: the OBS key, the pin, the package names and the binary all come from it.
      - name: Init renet submodule
        run: git submodule update --init --depth 1 private/renet

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}
      # opensuse/leap:16.0 comes from Docker Hub.
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          username: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Install oras
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image install-oras

      - name: Read the build OBS serves
        id: upstream
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror upstream

      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: 'stable'
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: private/renet/go.sum
      # A plain static `go build`, as the pkg matrix does: `renet ceph install`
      # needs no embedded assets, and the binary runs in the Leap container.
      # Never uploaded (console is public).
      - name: Build renet
        working-directory: private/renet
        run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet" ./cmd/renet

      # OBS's current build, pinned or not: capturing it before the pin moves is
      # what lets the pin move at all.
      - name: Capture the build OBS serves
        env:
          OBS_MIRROR_EVR: ${{ inputs.evr || steps.upstream.outputs.obs_evr }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror capture --evr "$OBS_MIRROR_EVR" --renet "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet"
      # The tree's pin: a no-op once captured, and red when it is neither
      # captured nor served any more.
      - name: Capture the pin
        if: steps.upstream.outputs.pin != (inputs.evr || steps.upstream.outputs.obs_evr)
        env:
          OBS_MIRROR_EVR: ${{ steps.upstream.outputs.pin }}
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.obs_mirror capture --evr "$OBS_MIRROR_EVR" --renet "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet"

name: VM Bake (${{ matrix.os-image }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # packages: write pushes the baked image to ghcr.io/rediacc/ci-vm-bake with
    # github.token. The first push (run 36670172753) created the package PUBLIC,
    # inheriting this public repository's visibility; the operator set it private
    # on 2026-09-30 (ruling D1) through the package settings page, the only place
    # that changes it, since no API sets package visibility.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os-image:
          - ubuntu-24.04
          - debian-13
          - fedora-43
          - opensuse-16.0
          - oracle-10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/profiler
        with:
          runner-label: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Fetch secrets from Bitwarden
        # LIVE: the BWS_ values below are read by this job's steps.
        uses: ./.github/actions/bws-secrets
        with:
          access-token: ${{ secrets.BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
          secrets: |
            GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY > BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
            DOCKERHUB_TOKEN > BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN
            DOCKERHUB_USERNAME > BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME
            GITHUB_APP_ID > BWS_APP_ID
      - uses: ./.github/actions/app-token
        id: app-token
        with:
          client-id: ${{ env.BWS_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ env.BWS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          preset: readonly
          repositories: console,renet
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
      # renet alone: the key hashes its sources and the build needs nothing else.
      - name: Init renet submodule
        run: git submodule update --init --depth 1 private/renet

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Install oras
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image install-oras
      # The early exit: a key that already has a package ends the leg here.
      - name: Probe the bake key
        id: probe
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image probe --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}"

      - name: Free Disk Space (start)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          username: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ env.BWS_DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        with:
          go-version: 'stable'
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: private/renet/go.sum
      # Same staged embed-assets cache as the E2E Workers legs (ci-build-renet.yml
      # writes it); restore only, the bake never saves it.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: embed-cache
        with:
          path: private/renet/pkg/embed/assets
          key: renet-embed-assets-${{ hashFiles('private/renet/embed-assets.lock.json') }}
      - name: Pre-pull Docker base images (avoid buildx auth issues)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false' && steps.embed-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.docker_prepull debian:bookworm=linux/amd64 debian:bookworm-slim=linux/arm64 ubuntu:24.04=linux/amd64 ubuntu:24.04=linux/arm64
      - name: Build renet
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.build_renet --nolicense
      - name: Install renet
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: sudo cp "$RENET_BINARY" /usr/bin/renet && sudo chmod +x /usr/bin/renet

      # The stock base image, from the cache the E2E Workers legs save (same key).
      # Restore only: on a miss the builder downloads it, and the E2E legs own the save.
      - name: Compute VM image cache key
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: vm-image-key
        run: echo "key=vm-base-image-e2e-${{ matrix.os-image }}-$(date -u +%Y-%m)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Restore VM base image cache
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/renet/disks
          key: ${{ steps.vm-image-key.outputs.key }}

      - name: Free Disk Space (wait)
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space
        with:
          mode: wait
      - name: Setup KVM Host
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: sudo "$RENET_BINARY" ops host setup

      - name: Bake the image
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        id: build
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image build --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}" --key "${{ steps.probe.outputs.key }}" --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/renet/disks-baked" --renet /usr/bin/renet
      - name: Publish to GHCR
        if: steps.probe.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.infra.vm_bake_image publish --distro "${{ matrix.os-image }}" --key "${{ steps.probe.outputs.key }}" --image "${{ steps.build.outputs.image }}"
